All frequently asked questions

The basics

Think of it as a personal helper that works for you around the clock. You message it like you'd text a friend, and it handles the task: checking your email, setting reminders, looking things up, and more. It's not a chatbot with canned responses. It actually does things.
None, and coding is entirely optional. We teach and guide you through setup in plain language, building on your own computer together. You can stay hands-off, hands-on, or somewhere in between. If you ever want to learn how it works under the hood, we’ll go as deep as you like at your own pace. If you’d rather not, that’s completely fine too.
You’ll understand it. That’s the point of guided setup: a real back-and-forth, not an install-and-goodbye. We walk through what the technology can and can’t do and why we make each choice, in plain language. You don’t need to become technical; you just walk away knowing your own agent well enough to keep imagining new things for it to do.
Most AI assistants live on someone else’s servers and bill you every month. Archie is the opposite. Your conversations and files stay on your own computer and go straight to the AI company on your own account, never through our servers. You pay the AI company directly, with no markup from us. You also stay in control: email waits for your Send tap, and it can’t spend money on its own (there is no purchase feature, and anything shaped like paying on a website is stopped and routed to you first). Most tools rent you an assistant they control; Otian hands you one that’s actually yours.
You wouldn’t. Keep the apps you like. An agent adds a layer of intelligence on top: an assistant that’s constantly looking out for you, so you don’t have to monitor everything yourself. Right now your apps only work when you check them, which is why the average worker bounces between 9 apps a day and toggles between them nearly 1,200 times, losing almost 4 hours a week just reorienting. Here’s what that looks like in practice: your car registration renewal sits in an email you skimmed 3 weeks ago. Your old setup waits for you to remember it. Your agent doesn’t. It catches the deadline, adds it to your list, and messages you before it lapses. Nothing you love changes. Your setup just gets a mind of its own.
Keep it. Archie isn’t a replacement, it’s a different kind of thing.

Most AI waits for work. Even the strong ones, the tools that genuinely go off and handle a real task, need you to bring the task first. It delivers, the job ends, and everything left over is still yours to remember.

Archie doesn’t wait. It runs on your own computer, on a schedule, whether you’re at your desk or asleep. The follow-up that never got a reply, flagged before you remembered it. The draft sitting in your chat with a Send button. Your morning laid out with your coffee. You don’t open Archie, Archie reaches you.

Most AI finishes tasks. Archie watches the stuff you never assigned.

And it’s yours in ways most AI isn’t: it remembers across weeks (tell it once, it holds onto it) and it runs under your own accounts, on your own computer, on one plan, with nothing routed through our servers once your own AI key is in.

If your problem is ”I have a hard task,” a work tool is the right call. If it’s ”small things keep slipping,” that’s Archie. Plenty of people end up wanting both.

Add-ons

They don’t talk to each other directly: your agent is the one that passes the work between them. Each add-on does its one job and hands the result back to your agent, which takes it from there, either passing it along to the next add-on to build on, or calling on several at once and combining what they send back. Every add-on stays focused on its own job; your agent is the one carrying the work from step to step and pulling the pieces into a single answer. Think of it like a kitchen line: each station handles one part of the dish, and your agent is the chef moving the plate from one station to the next and deciding what comes together.
Because “everything” isn’t one job: it’s hundreds of unrelated ones bundled under a single word. That’s exactly why you want many separate add-ons instead. Each handles one job well, so your agent can act sharply, reaching for the right one at the right moment instead of wading past the tax rules and the flight-booking steps just to find your dinner recipe. You still get everything: your agent simply picks the focused add-on that fits the moment. It’s a well-organized toolbox, not one giant gadget welded together.
Each add-on carries a short description of what it’s for. When you hand your agent a task, it scans those descriptions, picks the one that fits, and only then loads the full instructions. That’s why focused add-ons matter: clear, narrow descriptions make the right pick obvious.

Cost & billing

Getting started has 3 simple pieces:

Discovery call: free. 30 minutes covering your goals, what your agent should look like, and a rough timeline. No obligation.

Guided sessions: $250 an hour. The rate never rises with complexity; a bigger setup just takes more sessions, and we tell you how many on the free call.

Archie app: $30 a month, or $299 a year (at launch). A year costs $61 less than twelve months bought one at a time. Sold separately from sessions, and you can change or stop it whenever you like.
Yes, and there are 2 ways in.

Free credits. A new install comes with a small amount of AI usage we pay for, so you can watch an agent do something real before opening an account anywhere. They go to your Otian account once, they need a confirmed email address, and they are limited per computer: if someone has already used them on the computer you are on, Archie will tell you they have been claimed here rather than hand out a fresh set. While you are spending them, your messages pass through a server of ours on the way to Claude, because it is our account paying. That is the only time that ever happens, and it stops the moment you connect an AI account of your own.

Or 14 days on your own AI account. If the credits are gone, or you would rather they were never in the picture, connect an AI account of your own and you get a full fortnight. This is the one that is genuinely the whole app: on our credits your agent cannot read your email, because your mail would pass through our servers and the people who wrote to you never agreed to that, and connecting your own account turns every email tool on with nothing to switch. Because your key is paying for the thinking, your conversations go straight to the AI company you picked. We are never in the middle of them. That is Archie behaving exactly as it does for a paying customer, which makes it the more honest trial of the two.
No. The app is a plan of its own, $30 a month or $299 a year (at launch); guided sessions cover our time building your agent with you. They are priced separately because they are separate things, and a session is worth having whether or not you keep the app running afterwards.
Yes, on the app. Archie comes with a 14-day money-back guarantee: if it’s not for you, email us within 14 days of starting a plan and we’ll refund what you paid in full. After that, stopping a plan is self-serve from your account screen (a couple of clicks in the billing portal, no email needed) and takes effect at the end of the period you have already paid for. Guided sessions work differently, because they’re real hours we spend building alongside you, so that time isn’t refundable once we’ve done the work. It’s part of why the discovery call is free: you get a clear sense of the fit before you spend anything.
Yes, and for a personal agent it’s small. Archie connects to the AI (your pick of seven: Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Groq, Grok, DeepSeek or Mistral) through your own pay-as-you-go account, so you only pay for what your agent actually does: $1 to $7 a month for a handful of tasks a day, $41 to $63 for one you’re in all day with your calendar and inbox connected, and $112 to $204 for an agent worked hard and wired into most of your working day. Each is a range because the response quality you pick and how you space your messages out both move it, and on a light agent the quality setting alone is the difference between the two ends. You add a small amount of credit up front and can set a hard spending cap on the AI company’s website. During guided setup, we work with a standard AI subscription (like Claude Pro, around $20 a month) while we build; once you’re running Archie, the pay-as-you-go account takes over. Here’s where those figures come from, including which parts we measured and which we assumed. The figures went up in August 2026, and not because anything got dearer: they used to count the messages you send and the reports your agent runs, and not the mail it reads while you’re away.
Your subscription only works inside that company’s own app; it can’t be used by programs you own. Archie talks to the AI through your own API key (a private access code the AI company gives you, so Archie can connect on your account), a 2-minute setup the app walks you through. It’s the better deal anyway: you only pay for what you use (often less than a subscription), there are no daily usage caps, and the account is entirely yours. We never see it. On most of the companies Archie connects to, API traffic is not used to train the AI, but it depends on the provider and sometimes on whether the key is paid or free tier; our Trust page quotes each company on it. Your existing subscription keeps working as normal. How it works

Safety & privacy

Only the ones you approve. We go through everything with you before connecting anything, and you can revoke access at any time. Nothing gets linked without your explicit sign-off.
It can send email and text replies, but never on its own. It drafts the reply, hands it to you in the chat, and it goes out only when you tap Send. Calendar changes are proposed, held, and can only be applied exactly as proposed after your next message, never while you’re away. It proposes; you approve.

What it genuinely cannot do is spend money on its own: there is no purchase feature, and anything shaped like paying on a website is stopped and routed to you first. Buying an add-on is something you do yourself, through Stripe. And on its own your agent speaks only in the chats you’ve connected it to, and only to you, the person who paired with it; the one way its words reach anyone else is a draft, an email or text reply, that goes nowhere until you press Send. The current, honest list is on our Trust page.
Nothing is permanent: if something goes wrong, we fix or undo it, then fine-tune based on your feedback. Early mistakes are a normal, expected part of the process; that’s what the tuning period is for.
No. Archie runs on your own computer, and your agent’s instructions, uploaded files, chat history, and API key are all stored on your computer; the key is kept in your system’s own keychain (your computer’s built-in password store), where we can’t read it. Everything lives in a folder just for Archie; removing the app alone does not remove that folder or your keys (your computer keeps app data separate from apps), so to erase everything use the factory reset inside Archie, under Account. Otian AI does not store, read, or have any access to it. When your agent needs to think, it sends that request to the AI company you chose, on your account, with your key, the same way you already use Claude or ChatGPT. We are never in the middle of it. The one exception is the free credits Archie starts you with: those run on our own Anthropic account, so until you connect an AI account of your own, those requests pass through a server of ours, which forwards them and measures the spend without recording what was in them. Our servers hold your email address, whether you have a current plan, and which paid add-ons you’ve bought: the account and the receipt. Two more only where they apply: which version of Archie you are running, so we know what is still out there before we switch one off, and, if you turn on phone access, the messages between your computer and your phone, sealed with a key we never receive. The version line, and the crash report Archie sends if it breaks, can both be switched off in the app under Settings. When you add a free add-on, Archie bumps its public install count, but we keep no record of which ones are yours. A few smaller account records round it out (the free-credit ledger, second-factor records, invoices if you book a session), all listed in the privacy policy, and none holding anything you wrote.
Your agent’s data lives in a folder on your computer, protected by your computer’s own login and disk encryption, and your API key sits in the system keychain rather than in a file. If the computer is lost, revoking access takes minutes: reset your key on the AI company’s website and disconnect any linked accounts. Because nothing is copied to our servers, your own backup is what would restore it, so an agent you rely on is worth including in whatever backup you already run.

Timeline & what to expect

A first working version can often be live the same day, and most clients have one to three useful workflows running within the first week of completing the intake form, so you don’t need to wait for a perfect final version to start benefiting. From there, “setup” isn’t really a finish line. Most people keep building for weeks and months, adding accounts, tasks, and new ways of using it as they go.
Yes. This is the recommended path. Start with one or two high-value workflows, then add more once those are stable and saving you time.
If it can be done on a computer, your agent can probably learn to do it: inbox and calendar, research, bookkeeping, travel, health tracking, customer follow-ups, even building you a small tool. Day to day, some people get a morning briefing and a clean inbox; others let it quietly run parts of a business. The real question isn’t “can it do X”, it’s “what would make your life easier?” See it work
Tell us. We’ll scope it, quote it, and build the add-on. It’s yours, and it goes on the marketplace so the next person doesn’t have to ask. Commission an add-on to get started.
We handle the technical side completely, and once it’s running, it mostly takes care of itself. The more interesting part isn’t technical: it’s a conversation about what you want your agent trusted with, and that goes as far as you want: some clients keep it to one or two things done well, others keep expanding its responsibilities month after month. Either way, we stay available with ongoing guidance (from quick check-ins to deeper working sessions) whenever you want to adjust something or add the next capability.

Practical details

No. You need a computer you’re happy to leave on and keep connected to the internet; a Mac mini is the easy answer, never the requirement. Most people already own something that will do, and the machine spends most of its life idle, so it does not need to be fast or new. If you want that worked out for your own situation rather than in general, What to run it on asks a few questions and writes out the kit, including the parts you can skip and what your setup will not do. Archie is in testing on both Mac and Windows, and the waitlist hears the day it opens. See where it stands → The full list of what you’ll want ready is at What You Need.
Two different things, so here is both. If you stop your plan, Archie stops letting you in at the end of the period you have paid for; nothing on your computer is deleted, and starting a plan again puts everything back (in the rare case where the payment system books your return as a new customer, it can take an email to us first). Every add-on is included with Archie today, and if that ever changes, anything you bought outright stays bought. If we disappear, that is the one we have committed to in writing: our Terms require us to publish a final version that requires no license check, within 30 days of ceasing operations. Your account with the AI company and its key are separate from all of this and unaffected; you manage those directly with the provider you chose.
Whichever you already use: your agent replies right inside it, and you can switch later. Archie works with Telegram, Discord, Slack, Matrix and, on a Mac, iMessage; Telegram is the easiest to start with. You can also talk to your agent in Archie itself, on the computer it runs on, and it is the same conversation either way: write from your desk, carry on from your phone, and the answer appears in both. So there is no wrong pick, and no rush to make one.
Any of them works, and you can switch anytime, so this isn’t a decision you can get wrong. Archie connects to Anthropic (Claude), OpenAI (ChatGPT), Google (Gemini), Groq, xAI (Grok), DeepSeek, or Mistral, or to any other service with an OpenAI-format endpoint you name yourself. If you’re unsure, Claude is a great default: it’s what we build and test on, and it is what the free credits Archie starts you with run on. Want to try before adding billing of your own? That is what the free credits are for: they run on Claude and are already there, so none of these has to be connected on your first day.
Start on Balanced: it’s the sweet spot of cost and smarts for most people. Economy is quick and cheapest for simple tasks; Best uses the most capable model for high-stakes work at a higher cost per message. You can change the dial anytime.

One thing to know if you’re moving the dial to save money: an add-on can pick its own level and ignore the dial, and many do, so on an agent with several add-ons installed the dial alone barely changes the bill. The checkbox under it, “Use this for every skill”, is the one that overrides them. Measured on an agent with 12 add-ons, that checkbox takes about four fifths off the monthly cost. It also takes those add-ons off the level they chose, which is the trade.
Yes to both. Your agent runs on your own computer rather than on ours, so it can only do anything while that computer is powered on, awake, and connected to the internet. A computer that is on but has no internet connection cannot do the work either: it needs both.

A laptop is fine. Leave it plugged into power and set it never to sleep in your computer’s power settings, which we will do with you on a guided setup if you’d rather not hunt for it. For the connection, a wired Ethernet cable from your router to the computer is steadier than Wi-Fi, and we’d suggest it wherever you can run one: Wi-Fi drops out more often, and every drop is time your agent spends stopped. If Wi-Fi is what you have, keep the computer in range of the router rather than at the far end of the house.

If the computer shuts down, goes to sleep, or drops off the internet, your agent stops where it is. Once the computer is powered back on and connected again, it starts working again by itself: there is nothing for you to click and nothing to set up a second time.
